rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## The play at a glance "The Bull" by Bhimnidhi Tiwari is a Nepali one-act satire with a live animal at its centre: Mukundadixit, a farmer, keeps an unproductive bull although the government has banned keeping bulls that serve no purpose — the state's campaign to control stray and useless cattle.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Satire on superstition: villagers fear a bull as 'Bhairav' — ignorance exploited.
Laxmi's courage exposes the fraud; theme of reason vs blind faith.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Trick 3: Comedy technique: escalating chaos and mistaken reports — pick two comic moments and their targets.  ·  ## The characters worth an essay **Mukundadixit** is the satirist's specimen: pious in language, practical in motive — his defence of the bull is a costume over convenience, and his skill is exactly the skill the inspection rewards: fluency in deference. The sketch the exam wants holds the double reading: the tradition-keeper who is really a rule-dodger, and the rule-dodger who half-believes his own piety.…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: ## The themes worth an essay **Tradition as convenience** — the central theme: the bull kept in religion's name and convenience's interest; the play distinguishes belief from the costume of belief. **Law and its performance** — the conceptual heart: the inspection defeated by flattery and staging; the theme that enforcement which accepts deference collects nothing.…  ·  ## NEB short answers, solved **Q. Why does Mukundadixit keep the bull against the law? (2 marks)** A. For prestige, tradition and convenience: the bull is a status animal in the village's eyes, its keeping is defended in religious language, and obeying the government's campaign would cost him trouble he prefers to avoid. Piety is the costume; convenience is the motive. **Q.…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. What social evils does the play mock? (2 marks) — superstition and the dowry system; the family's panic over omens.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ## NEB long answers, solved **Q. "The Bull is a satire on both the law-dodgers and the law-enforcers." Discuss. (8 marks)** A model answer works both edges with the play's evidence: the farmer's side — the bull kept in religion's name and convenience's interest, the household coached, the pious language deployed over a practical motive; and the officials' side — procedure satisfied by tea, flattery and smooth…  ·  **‘The Bull’ — satire of superstition (classified)** | Element | Detail | Satire target | |---|---|---| | Mukundaprasad | Fears the bull | Cowardly superstition | | Bull’s rampage | Village chaos | Panic without reason | | Men hiding | Clerks, officers | Male bravado exposed | | Women’s courage | They face it down | Gender role reversal |

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## The action, scene by scene The setup is the household and its secret: Mukundadixit keeps the bull against the law and justifies it in the traditional grammar — the bull as God's creature, the farm's prestige, the ancestors' custom — while the practical truth is simpler: he does not want the expense and trouble of obeying, and he believes he will not be caught.…  ·  ## The devices, with evidence - **Satire** — the play's genre and method: the bull campaign as a duel between hypocrisy and officialdom, with both sides laughing at themselves. - **Dramatic irony** — the audience's position: we see the bull, the coaching and the lie while the officials see only the performance — every deferential sentence the inspectors accept is a sentence the audience knows to be false.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Social satire: Laxminarayan's superstition and dowry-driven panic are mocked through the runaway bull — name the customs the play satirises.  ·  Trick 2: The bull as plot device: one animal exposes every character's fear and greed — analyse the bull's symbolic function.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. What role does the bull play in the plot? (2 marks) — its escape triggers the chaos that reveals each character's true nature.
